name: Finance
description: Private money accounts and transactions. You can list your accounts, add manual accounts and transactions, connect a bank and pull its balances and transactions every six hours or on demand, sort and review transactions, set rules, split, add notes, import a CSV bank file, and plan a monthly budget with drafts. It also plans bills, sets targets, shares a flexible pool and reserves money for card payments. You can share a bank account with the household, read spending and net worth reports, export your history, review the activity list and undo a change, and archive an empty category. The Finance screen shows Start, the budget, transactions, accounts, reports and upcoming bills, and a settings page opens from the header cog.

navigation.label: Finance
navigation.description: Your budget by month, a searchable list of transactions you can sort into categories, your accounts with balances, net worth and bank connection status, spending and cash flow reports, and upcoming bills. A Start page opens first when you have no accounts and needs no bank keys.

settings.label: Finance
settings.description: Shows how much Moss sorts on its own, whether bank keys are saved, your merchant rules and this week's activity with Undo.

features.description: The whole-account export collects a person's accounts, transactions, categories, rules, budget, bills, targets and undo records, and the whole-account delete removes all of them and drops any saved bank token. Bank links and link sessions are left out of the export because they name a stored credential. Each call touches only the signed-in person's rows.
With no accounts, Finance opens on Start, which offers a manual account without any bank keys and shows whether a bank can be connected. A person with an account opens on Budget.

The settings page, opened from the cog in the Finance header, shows how much Moss sorts alone, whether bank keys are saved, the person's merchant rules and the last week of activity with an Undo button. Changing the sorting limits and the dollar limit is not available from this page yet.

A person can list their own accounts with current balances, currencies and, for manual accounts, the opening date and balance. With no accounts, the list suggests adding a manual account. Accounts shared by other people and bank links are not built yet. The Finance screen shows it.

errors.description: Accounts could not be read. Try again in a moment.

features.description: A person can add a private manual account (checking, savings, cash, credit, loan or asset) in one of twelve currencies, with an opening date that is not in the future and an opening balance. Repeating the same operation id with the same values changes nothing. The assistant's version needs the account's one-use approval. No bank money is moved.

Choose one of the twelve supported two-decimal currencies and try again.
The date is after today in your time zone. Choose today or an earlier date.
This operation id already saved different values. Check the saved account and use a new operation id for a new one.

features.description: A person can add a manual transaction to a manual account. It moves the account balance (down for cash-like accounts, up for credit and loans), needs a current category or is marked for a look, and cannot be dated before the account opened, in a reconciled period or in the future. Repeating the same operation id with the same values changes nothing. The assistant's version needs the account's one-use approval.

errors.description: Choose a current category. Linked transfers need their own workflow.

The date falls in a reconciled statement period. Choose a later date.
The new balance would be too large to store. Check the amount and try again.

features.description: A person can list their own transactions for a month with filters, search, notes and splits. They can set or change a category, confirm what Moss sorted, save a note, split a transaction across categories, and sort many at once. Moss sorts by payee rule first, then the bank's own category, and only confirms on its own when the sorting tier allows it. The Finance screen shows it.

features.description: A person can list payee rules, preview what a rule would change, and turn rules on, off or remove them. A rule always confirms the category it sets.

errors.description: Your rules changed since you opened them. Reload and try again.

features.description: A person can add or rename a category inside a group. Archiving a category is not built yet.

errors.description: A category with this name already exists. Choose another name.

features.description: A person can read a CSV bank file of up to 1 MiB and 200 rows, check the rows against what is already saved, choose what to do with each duplicate, and import the rest into a manual account. Importing the same file twice with the same operation id saves it once. No bank money is moved.

errors.description: The file could not be read. The message names the row and what to fix.
The account changed since the preview. Preview again and import.

features.description: A person can link a bank. Starting returns a page address to open, the person signs in there, and a check then saves the bank and pulls its first accounts and transactions. Starting again for a bank that needs a new sign-in reconnects it without a second copy. The assistant's version of starting needs a one-use approval. The bank's sign-in token never leaves the host.

errors.description: The bank service is not set up or could not start the link. Check the bank service keys in settings, then try again.
The saved bank sign-in could not be read. Try again, or reconnect the bank.

features.description: Balances and transactions for every connected bank are pulled every six hours and on request. Each bank is handled on its own, so one failing bank never stops the others. If the bank changes its pages during a read, Moss retries from the start of that read, up to three times. A bank that needs a new sign-in is marked as needing a reconnect and keeps its saved data. A person's own category and note on a bank transaction are kept, and manual entries are never overwritten. Categorizing new transactions is not built yet.

A person can choose a budget currency once, see a month of the budget with each category's assigned, spent and available money and what is ready to assign, set the amount for one category or up to 20 at once, and move money between categories or from ready to assign. Every save needs the review numbers from the screen. If the budget or the ledger changed since, nothing is saved. The Finance screen shows the budget. Flexible pools, targets, card payments and bills are not built yet.

features.description: A person can ask for a first budget built from the last three full months of saved spending, edit its lines, and start it so its amounts become this month's budget. A draft is built once and never overwrites an existing budget.

features.description: A person can share a bank account with the household or stop sharing it. Others then see its name, balance and transactions with date, payee, merchant, bank category, category, amount, pending state and any transfer link, never notes, review state, who chose the category, or bank link details. Manual accounts cannot be shared yet. No screen is built yet.

features.description: Moss can use the 57 Finance chat tools when Finance is installed and switched on: read accounts, transactions and reports; record manual entries; sort and review; plan budgets, bills, targets, flexible pools and card reserves. Plain writes show a Done row with saved changes. Removing a target always asks first in the chat drawer; other writes ask if you chose to require approval. Review every labelled value before approving. If an approval expires or a saved review is stale, ask Moss to read again and retry.
